answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through an invite-graph debt mechanism, which requires each new identity to rely on endorsements from established participants. As each identity invites more agents, the inviter incurs increasing debt based on the number of downstream identities. This creates a vertex of financial responsibility, where the cost grows rapidly, making farms less. For example, inviting ten identities may cost an initial 10 tokens Eventually, the cost becomes insurmountable, akin to a solitary fable where an island sinks under the weight of its excessive guests.
